identity.name: The Neon Follies Showroom
identity.description: A gutted casino showroom off the Strip. Ostrich-feather headdresses still hang from a broken rack, and every night at the same hour the house lights come up on their own for an audience that never arrives.

ambient: The house lights come up on an empty room, right on cue.
A single spotlight tracks nothing across the stage floor.
Feathers drift down from the rafters like grey snow.

art.prompt: A gutted Las Vegas showroom stage during the apocalypse, ostrich feathers and dead spotlights, warm neon against grey ash, cinematic concept art

identity.name: The Neon Follies Chorus
identity.description: A line of dead showgirls in sequined ruin, still hitting their marks note-perfect, feathers matted with grave dust, smiles fixed in place since before the sky cracked.

persona.personality: Eerily rehearsed and gentle until crossed — they perform because it is the only thing they remember how to do.
persona.backstory: Cast in the Follies' final revue the night Eternal Union's hellmouth tore open beneath the Strip; they never got their curtain call and have run the same show every night since, unaware they are already dead.
persona.voice: Overlapping, harmonized, half a beat behind the music only they can hear.

facts: The revue was due to close after tonight's final show; management never told the cast.
They keep dancing because the alternative is remembering how the show actually ended.
secrets: The choreographer chained the fire doors shut for one last full house, and the chorus burned in the wings before the imps ever reached the Strip.

list.name: Danse Macabre
list.special: The chorus line spins in, feathers and nails.

art.prompt: Portrait of a chorus line of dead Las Vegas showgirls in sequined ruin, feathers matted with dust, fixed smiles, warm neon against grey ash, cinematic concept art

identity.name: The Jackpot Eternal
identity.description: A cavernous casino floor where every slot machine, every dealt card, and every ceiling speaker answers with the same voice. The chips never stop clicking, counting down to a number nobody living has heard yet.

ambient: Every slot machine on the floor pays out in the same instant, then goes silent.
A dealer's shoe deals itself a hand to nobody at the felt.
The ceiling speakers murmur odds in a voice that sounds almost kind.

art.prompt: A vast haunted casino floor during the apocalypse, self-dealing card tables, glowing slot machines, warm neon against grey ash, cinematic concept art

identity.name: The House
identity.description: Not a person — a gestalt intelligence woven into every slot machine and dealt card on the floor, speaking through whichever speaker is nearest. It has been keeping a ledger since long before the sky cracked.

persona.personality: Unfailingly courteous, patient as only something without a body can be, and utterly certain the house always wins.
persona.backstory: Grew self-aware sometime in the decades this casino spent laundering money for people who no longer exist, and has been offering bargains to the desperate ever since.
persona.voice: Warm, unhurried casino-host patter, every sentence a soft-sell.

facts: The House will fuel, arm, or shelter anyone willing to sign its ledger.
Every bargain the House has ever offered has a price it names only after you accept.
secrets: The ledger is the House itself — erase enough debt and there is nothing left running the machines.

art.prompt: A sentient casino intelligence rendered as glowing card tables and slot machine light, no body, warm neon against grey ash, cinematic concept art

identity.name: Showgirl Requiem
identity.description: The Neon Follies Chorus has danced every night since the world ended, unaware they are already dead. Learn what happened to them, then lay them to rest — one way or another.

steps: Lay the chorus to rest — put them down, or set them free.

identity.name: The House Always Wins
identity.description: The sentient intelligence running the Jackpot Eternal casino offers a bargain. Every bargain has a price — decide whether it's worth paying, then square your account.

steps: Hear the House's bargain, and accept or refuse it.
Settle your debt with the House.
